verdict.summary: SPEC-0336: pre-slot signals no longer raise inside a lock release or a running git, stale git lock files in the worker cache are cleared, and the concurrent-jobs test pins slots: 2. Before the slot stage, the signal handler only records a SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP. It raises at once only while the job is blocked reading stdin; anywhere else the job raises it at the next check between steps. A signal therefore cannot leave a flock held (which deadlocked the job's own cleanup) or SIGKILL a git mid ref-update. Every git that writes the cache runs under the repo lock, so checkout, have and gc now delete leftover git `.lock` files before they write.

followup_ideas: A long bundle fetch or a large cache update runs to completion before a pre-slot signal takes effect. If that delay matters, make the cache fetch cancellable by sending git a SIGTERM (git removes its own lock files on SIGTERM).
The repo lock and jobs lock are blocking flocks with no timeout. A diagnostic (who holds it, for how long) in `nw worker info` would help operators debug a stuck worker.
